detailed_findings.finding: The forward construction from a numerical semigroup S to the tuple x(S) is correct: nonemptiness of each residue class uses finiteness of the complement, positivity x_r >= 1 uses multiplicity m, and the two Kunz inequalities are derived correctly from minimality in each residue class.

The genus computation for S is complete: the proof identifies exactly the gaps in each nonzero residue class and uses closure under addition with m to show all integers in a residue class above w_r belong to S.

The reverse construction S(x) is correct and sufficiently justified: finite complement, multiplicity m, and closure under addition are all established with the necessary residue-case split, including the separate i+j=m case.
The inverse-map verification is complete: from S one recovers exactly the threshold description S(x), and from x one recovers the same least representatives m x_r + r in each residue class.
There is no semantic drift: the proof proves exactly the stated cardinality equality and uses notions consistent with the lemma and root theorem sketches.

reason: The proof gives a standard and complete bijection between numerical semigroups of multiplicity m and genus g and Kunz-coordinate tuples in K_{m,g}. It correctly constructs the forward map via the least element in each nonzero residue class modulo m, verifies positivity, the two inequality families, and the genus sum formula. It then defines the inverse set S(x), proves finite complement, multiplicity m, closure under addition by exhaustive residue-class analysis, and computes the genus. Finally it proves both compositions are identities. The argument matches the semantic sketch exactly and is well aligned with the root theorem’s counting interpretation.
